description: Each row represents a perpetrator of an act, identified by a unique id. It records the date, year, location, and details of how many were killed or injured. It links to the person responsible for the act.
Each row represents a person, recording their name, height, weight and hometown. It links to the perpetrator table to identify potential suspects.
Each row represents a classroom, identified by its building and room number. It records the classroom's capacity. It links to departments that use it and to course sections held there.

Each row represents a college department, listing its name, the building it is in, and its annual budget. It links to classrooms by building and connects to courses, instructors, and students associated with the department.

Each row represents a college course, including its ID, title, department and credit hours. It links to the department that offers the course and sections that schedule it. Joining this table allows finding related sections and prerequisites.

Each row represents an instructor (a teacher) and includes their ID, name, department, and salary. It links to the department table for the instructor's department. Joining with the teaches table shows which courses they teach, and with the advisor table identifies their advising relationships.

Each row represents a section of a course (a class offering). It records the course ID, section ID, semester, year, building, room number, and time slot. It links to the course details, classroom information, and teaching schedule, allowing you to find which courses are offered in specific semesters and rooms.

Each row represents a teaching assignment, recording an instructor's course section and the semester and year it was taught. It links to instructors, courses, sections, and their semesters and years, showing which instructors teach what courses in which sections.

Each row represents a student and includes their ID, name, department, and total credits earned. It links to the department table for the student's academic department. Joining with these tables provides details on courses taken and assigned advisors.

Each row records a class taken by a student, including the course ID, section ID, semester, and grade. It links to the student who took the class and to the section of the course. Joining it with other tables allows tracking which students are enrolled in specific sections during particular semesters.
Each row records the advising relationship between a student and an instructor. It links to the student and instructor IDs, showing which instructors advise which students.
Each row represents a time slot for scheduling events, noting the day and start and end times. It links to course sections to define when classes are held.
Each row records a prerequisite for a course, linking the course that requires it to the course that is a prerequisite. It shows which courses are required before others can be taken.

Each row represents an airport, identified by its unique ID. It includes the city and country, along with IATA and ICAO codes and the airport's name. Airports are linked to flights that take off or land there.

Each row represents an operating company that runs flights. It records the company's name, type of operation, main activities, country of incorporation, and group equity shareholding. Flights reference it to identify which company operates them.

Each row represents a flight, recording its ID, flight number, date, pilot, velocity, altitude, and the airports it uses. It links to the operating company and the airports involved, providing details about each flight's route and crew.

Each row represents an institution, identified by a unique ID. It records the institution's name and country. It links to the authorship table to show which authors are affiliated with each institution.
Each row represents an author, with their unique identifier, last name, and first name. It links to the authorship table, which records the works they have authored.
Each row is a research paper submitted to the ICFP conference, identified by a unique ID. It records the paper's title. The table links to another table that associates authors with papers.
Each row records an author's contribution to a research paper, including their order of authorship. It links to the author, institution, and paper they contributed to.

Each row represents a bodybuilder and their performance in weightlifting. It records the bodybuilder's ID, their personal bests for snatch, clean and jerk, and their total lift. It links to the person's details in the people table.
Each row represents a person, recording their ID, name, height, weight, birth date, and birthplace. It links to other tables through the people_id field, allowing related data to be joined.

Each row represents a recorded storm, including its ID, name, active dates, maximum wind speed, estimated damage in millions of USD, and number of deaths. It links to regions affected by the storm, allowing you to see which storms impacted specific areas.
Each row represents a geographic region, identified by a code and named. It links to the regions affected by storms, showing which storms hit each area.

Each row represents an affected region during a storm, recording the region's ID and the number of cities impacted. It links to the storm that caused the impact and to the regions table for more details.

Each row represents an aircraft, recording its order year, manufacturer, model, and details like the powertrain and fuel type. It links to the pilot record table, providing information on which aircraft are flown by pilots.

Each row represents a pilot, recording their name, rank, age, nationality, position, the year they joined, and which team they are on. It links to itself, allowing detailed records of each pilot's information.
Each row records a pilot's flight, linking a pilot to an aircraft and the date of the flight. It helps track which pilots flew which aircraft on specific dates.
Each row represents a horse racing event (a race). It records the race's unique identifier, its name, class, and date. It links to the track where the race was held.
Each row represents a race track, including its unique identifier, name, location, seating capacity, and the year it opened. It links to races held at that track.

Each row represents an author, with their unique ID, homepage, and name. It links to the organization they are associated with and is linked from tables recording domains they write in and works they have written.

Each row represents a conference, identified by a unique code. It holds the conference's name and its homepage. It is linked to domains that categorize conferences and publications associated with them.

Each row represents a subject domain (field of study) identified by a unique code. It records the domain's name. This table is linked to other tables that connect domains to authors, conferences, journals, keywords, and publications, allowing searches across related academic information.
Each row records the association between an author and a domain of study. It links to the author and the domain, showing which authors work in which fields.

Each row records the relationship between a conference and its domain. It includes the conference ID (cid) and the domain ID (did). It links to the conferences and domains tables, showing which conferences belong to which domains.

Each row represents a journal (a periodical for publishing academic papers). It records the journal's unique identifier, its name, and its homepage. It is linked to domains and publications, allowing connections between journals and their fields of study, as well as articles published in them.

Each row links a domain to a journal, indicating which journals belong to each academic domain. It records the domain ID and the journal ID. It connects to domains and journals, showing their relationship.

Each row is a keyword used in academic publications. It records the keyword and its unique identifier (kid). It links to other keywords related to domains and publications, allowing connections between topics and papers.

Each row links a domain to its keywords. It records the domain ID and keyword ID, establishing which keywords describe each domain. It connects to domains and keywords, allowing searches across subjects and terms.

Each row represents a published academic paper, including its title, abstract, citation number, and year. It links to the conference or journal where it was published and connects to related tables for domains, keywords, authors, and citations.

Each row records a publication within a specific academic domain. It links the publication's unique identifier (pid) to its domain (did). Joining it allows finding publications by domain and vice versa.

Each row represents an academic organization, identified by a unique ID. It records the organization's name, its location on a continent, and its homepage. It is linked to authors who are affiliated with these organizations.

Each row links a publication to a keyword. It records the publication ID and the keyword ID, with the primary key being the keyword ID. It connects publications to their associated keywords, allowing searches by topic.

Each row records an authorship of a publication, linking an author to a paper or book. It includes the author's ID and the publication's ID. This table connects authors to their publications and vice versa.
Each row records a citation where one publication references another. It links to the publications that are cited and that do the citing, showing which papers reference each other.
Each row is an address, recording the full details of a location. It links to supplier and customer addresses, allowing those records to reference this one for consistency.
Each row represents a store employee, recording their ID, gender, and name. It links to the table that assigns employees to departments.

Each row represents a supplier of goods, identified by a unique ID. It records the supplier's name and phone number. It links to additional addresses for the supplier and to products supplied by them.
Each row represents a department store chain, identified by an ID and its name. It links to the stores in that chain.

Each row represents a customer, including their payment method code, name, address, phone number, and email. It links to additional addresses associated with the customer and to orders they have placed.

Each row represents a product sold in the department store, including its ID, type code, name, and price. It links to suppliers who provide the products and is referenced by orders that record which products are bought.

Each row records an address for a supplier, with the start and end dates of its validity. It links to the supplier and the specific address used. Joining it provides details on which addresses were used by each supplier over time.

Each row is an address associated with a customer. It records the start and end dates for when this address was valid. It links to the customer and their addresses, showing which addresses were used by each customer over time.

Each row is a customer order (an order placed with the store). It records the order ID, the customer who placed it, the order status and the date. It links to the customer and connects to the items ordered in the transaction.

Each row represents a department store, identified by its unique ID. It records the store's name, address, phone number, and email. It links to the department store chain it belongs to and is linked from the table that lists its departments.

Each row represents a department within a store, identified by its ID. It records the department's name and which store it belongs to. It links to staff assignments, showing which employees are assigned to each department.
Each row represents an item in a customer's order. It records the order item ID, the associated order ID, and the product ID. It links to the customer's order and the product being ordered.

Each row records a supplier for a product, including the dates they supplied it and the total amount and value purchased. It links to the products table to identify the specific item and to the suppliers table to track which company provided it.

Each row records a staff member's assignment to a department, including the start and end dates. It notes their job title code. It links to staff and departments, showing which employees work in each department and what roles they have.
Each row represents a musician or band identified by an ID. It includes the artist's name, age, and details of their most famous work including its title and release date.

Each row represents a music volume issue, including its ID, issue number, and release date. It also notes how many weeks the featured song was on top. The artist who performed the song is linked to their ID. Joining this table with music_festival allows finding which volumes were played at festivals.
Each row represents a music festival event, including its name, date, category, volume it appears in, and the result. It links to the volume where details are stored.
Each row represents a customer of the insurance company, recording their ID and name. It links to the policies they have, showing which customers are associated with which policies.
Each row represents a service provided in an insurance claim. It records the service's unique ID and its name. It is linked to claims to show which services were involved in each one.

Each row represents an insurance policy available for purchase. It records the policy's unique identifier, its type, and the customer's phone number. It links to the table that tracks which policies a customer has.

Each row represents a customer's insurance policy, noting when the policy was opened and closed. It links to the customer and the specific policy details, allowing connections to other tables that track claims or notifications related to these policies.

Each row is the first notification of a loss (an insurance claim). It records the customer and policy involved, along with the service provided. It links to the customer and policy details and the service type. Joining it allows tracking claims from this initial report.

Each row represents an insurance claim, identified by a unique claim ID. It records the claim's effective date and links to its corresponding first notification of loss (FNOL). Joining it with settlements shows which claims have been settled.

Each row is a settlement (an agreed payment) for an insurance claim. It records the settlement's ID, the related claim ID, the effective date, and the settlement amount. It links to the claim it resolves, providing details of when and how much was settled.

Each row is a film, identified by its ID. It records the film's rank in series, title, director, original air date and production code. It links to the schedule table, showing which films are shown at what times.
Each row represents a cinema, including its ID, name, opening year, seating capacity and location. It links to the schedule table, showing which films are shown there.

Each row represents a scheduled showing of a film at a cinema. It records the date, number of show times per day, and ticket price. It links to the cinema and the film, providing details on when and where a film is shown.

Each row represents a college participating in the decoration competition. It records the college's ID, name, leader's name, and location. It links to members of the college who are part of the competition.

Each row represents a competition member, recording their ID, name, country, and the college they belong to. It links to rounds to show which members participated in each round and connects back to colleges.

Each row represents a participant's entry in a competition round, recording their ID, the chosen theme and their ranking. It links to the member who submitted the entry and shows how they performed in that specific round.
Each row represents a mobile phone model, with its name, unique ID, memory capacity in gigabytes, carrier, and price. It connects to the phone market table for pricing information.

Each row represents a market in the phone market database. It records details like district, number of employees, number of shops, and a ranking. It links to itself, allowing related data to be joined for more detailed analysis.

Each row represents a market's inventory of phones, noting the number of each phone model in stock. It links to the market and the phone models it sells, allowing you to see which markets carry specific phones and how many are available.

Each row is a product (likely an office machine like a printer) sold in stores. It records the product name, dimensions, resolution, color print speed, maximum paper size and interface type. It links to other products for related information.

Each row represents a store, recording its ID, name, type, area size, number of product categories and ranking. It links to the district where the store is located and is referenced by tables tracking products in the store and districts.

Each row represents a district, identified by its ID. It records the district's name, the city where it is headquartered, and the city's population and area. The district table connects to stores within that district.
Each row records which products are available at a store. It links to the store and the product, showing the relationship between them.
Each row records the relationship between a store and its district. It links to the store and district IDs, showing which stores are in which districts.

Each row represents a third-party company involved in asset maintenance, including its type, name, address, and additional details. It links to maintenance contracts, asset suppliers, and maintenance engineers, providing information on who is responsible for various aspects of asset management.

Each row represents a maintenance contract, identifying the company responsible and the dates of the contract. It includes additional details about the contract. It links to the company that provides maintenance services and is linked from asset records to show which assets are covered by each contract.

Each row is a maintenance part, recording its name and whether it's chargeable. It includes the chargeable amount and any other relevant details about the part. It links to assets that use this part and to faults that involve this part.
Each row represents a maintenance skill, identified by a unique ID. It includes the skill's code and description. It is linked to engineers' skills and to tasks requiring specific skills.
Each row represents a maintenance staff member. It includes their name, gender, and additional details. It links to records of faults they logged and visits they conducted.

Each row represents an asset owned by the company, including its ID, maintenance contract details, supplier information, and acquisition and disposal dates. It links to maintenance contracts and suppliers, and connects to parts related to the asset and faults logged for it.
Each row records that an asset uses a specific part. It links to the asset and the part, showing which assets have which components.

Each row represents a maintenance engineer, including their ID, the company they work for, and their first and last names. It links to the company that employs them and records their other details. Joining it with related tables shows which skills engineers have and the visits they make.
Each row records an engineering skill held by a maintenance engineer. It links to the engineer and the specific skill, showing which engineers have which skills.

Each row logs a reported fault for an asset, including when it was logged, who reported it, and details of the fault. It links to the asset and the staff member who recorded the fault, and connects to records of engineer visits and replacement parts related to these faults.

Each row records an engineer's visit to check or fix equipment. It includes details like the start and end times, the status of any faults found, and notes on other activities. It links to the staff member contacted, the engineer who visited, and the fault log entry related to the visit.

Each row records a fault or issue with a specific part, noting the part's ID, a short name for the fault, its full description, and any additional details. It links to the parts table to identify the faulty component and connects to logs of faults and required skills for fixing them.

Each row logs a specific part's fault within a maintenance entry. It records the fault status of the part. It links to the overall fault log and to the specific part that has a fault, allowing details of each part's maintenance issues to be tracked.
Each row records a skill required to fix a specific part or fault. It links to the part fault and the skill, showing which skills are needed for each repair task.
Each row is an address, recording the full postal details including line 1, line 2, city, zip code, state or province, and country. It links to people who are associated with that address.

Each row represents a person, likely a student or staff member, with their first name, last name, contact details and login information. It links to other tables like students, addresses, and candidates, providing a central record for personal data.

Each row represents a student, with their unique identifier and basic details. It links to the people table for full details of each person. Joining it allows tracking students in course registrations.

Each row represents a course offered, with its ID, name, and a brief description. It includes any additional relevant information. It is referenced by the student course registrations table to track which courses students are enrolled in.
Each row records an address for a person, with the start and end dates of when it was their primary address. It links to the person and the address details.
Each row records a student's registration for a course, including the registration date. It links to the student and the course, and connects to related tables that track attendance.
Each row records a student's attendance at a course on a specific date. It links to the student and the course, showing which students attended which courses and when.

Each row represents a candidate taking an assessment, with their ID and details. It links to the person table for more information about the candidate. Assessments refer to it to record which candidates took part.

Each row represents an assessment result for a student. It records the qualification assessed, the date of the assessment and the outcome. It links to the student who was assessed, providing their ID.
Each row represents a dog breed, identified by a code and named in plain text. It links to the dogs table to show which breeds are kept in the kennels.
Each row represents a type of charge (such as boarding or grooming). It records the charge type and its associated amount.
Each row defines a kennel size, with a unique code and description. It links to the dogs table to specify the size of each dog's kennel.
Each row describes a type of treatment (e.g., vaccination, grooming) with a unique code and description. It links to the treatments table, allowing details of specific treatments given to dogs.
Each row represents an owner of a dog at the kennel. It includes the owner's name, address, contact information and email. It links to the dogs owned by that person.

Each row represents a dog in the kennel, including its ID, owner, breed, size, name, age, gender, weight, and dates of arrival, adoption, or departure. It links to the owner's ID, breed code, and size code for more details. Treatments refer to it to record which dogs received them.

Each row represents a professional at the dog kennels, including their role, contact details and personal information. It links to the treatments table to show which professionals provided care or treatment.

Each row records a treatment given to a dog, including the type of treatment, the date, and cost. It links to the dog receiving the treatment, the professional providing it, and the type of treatment administered.
Each row represents a music genre, noting its name, popularity rating, and the year it was most popular. It is referenced to find an artist's preferred genre and the genres of songs.

Each row represents an artist, including their name, country of origin, gender, and preferred music genre. It links to the genre table for more details on the artist's preferred style and is connected to songs and file records that attribute music to them.
Each row is a music file (a song) with details like the artist, file size, and duration. It links to the artist who performed the song and is referenced by another table that lists specific songs.
Each row represents a song, including its name, artist, country of origin, genre, rating, languages sung in, release date and file resolution. It links to the artist, genre and associated files.

Each row represents an employee of the company, recording their personal details such as name, age, nationality and highest education. It links to the employment table to show job roles and durations.

Each row represents a company, including its name, headquarters location, industry, and financial metrics like sales, profits, assets, and market value. It links to the employment table, showing which employees work for each company.
Each row records an employee's work at a company, noting the years they worked. It links to the company and the person employed, showing which employees worked for each company and when.
Each row represents a city, including its official name, status, area in square kilometers, population and census ranking. It links to the host city for farm competitions.

Each row represents a farm's livestock count for a specific year. It records the total number of horses, working horses, cattle, oxen, bulls, cows, pigs, and sheep and goats on the farm. This data helps track the farm’s animal population over time. Competition records refer to it to show which farms participated in events.
Each row represents a farm competition, including its unique ID, year, theme, and the host city. It links to the city hosting the event and records details in the competition history table.

Each row records a farm's ranking in a competition. It includes the competition ID, the farm ID, and the rank achieved. It links to the competition and the farm, allowing you to see which farms won or placed in specific competitions.
Each row is an address, recording the full details of a location. It links to events that occur at these locations, providing the address for each event.
Each row represents a location, identified by a unique ID. It includes additional details about the location. It is linked to events that occur at these locations.
Each row represents a financial product, identified by a unique ID. It records the product's type code, name and price. It is referenced by events that involve these products.
Each row represents a party involved in an event, identified by a unique ID. It holds details about the party. It links to and from the parties_in_events table, showing events involving each party.
Each row represents an asset held by a company. It includes additional details about the asset. It links to events where the asset is involved, allowing tracking of asset movements and usage.

Each row represents a distribution channel used to sell insurance products. It includes additional details about the channel. It links to events that involve these channels, showing which products were sold through each channel.
Each row holds financial information for a specific entity, including additional details. It links to the events table to provide context for financial changes or decisions.

Each row represents an event (such as a transaction or incident) recorded in the system. It includes details like the address, channel, type of event, finance ID, and location involved. It links to addresses, channels, finances, and locations for more context. Events are referenced by products, parties, agreements, and assets associated with them.
Each row records a financial product involved in an event. It links to the event and the product, showing which products are part of which events.

Each row records a party's role in an event, identified by the party and event IDs. It lists roles such as issuer or guarantor. It links to parties and events, showing which parties are involved in each event and their roles.
Each row represents an agreement, identified by a document ID. It links to an event that triggered the agreement.
Each row records an asset involved in a specific event. It links to the asset and the event, showing which assets are part of which events.

Each row represents a city, including its ID, name in English and Chinese, pronunciation, population, and GDP. It links to temperature data for the city and records which city hosted an event or competition.

Each row represents a sports match, recording its unique ID, date, venue, scores of teams involved, and the final result. It also notes which competition the match was part of. Hosting cities refer to it to show which matches were hosted.

Each row records monthly average temperatures for a city. It includes the temperature averages for each month from January to December. It links to the city table, providing temperature data for each city listed.

Each row records which city hosted a match in a given year. It includes the year, the match's ID and the name of the hosting city. It links to matches and cities, allowing you to find all matches hosted by a specific city or all cities that hosted a particular match.
Each row represents a swimmer, recording their name, nationality and best times for various distances in meters. It links to records that show the swimmer's achievements.
Each row represents a swimming stadium, recording its unique ID, name, capacity, location city and country. It also notes when the stadium opened. Other tables link to it to find events held there.

Each row represents a swimming event, identified by an ID. It records the event's name, the stadium where it was held, and the year of the competition. It links to the stadium and is linked from a table tracking event records.
Each row is a swimming record (a race result). It includes the result, the swimmer involved, and the event. It links to the swimmer and the event, connecting records to swimmers and races.
Each row represents an airline, including its unique ID, full name, abbreviation and country of origin. It links to the flights table to show which airlines operate which flights.

Each row represents an airport, listing its city, full name, and the country it's in. It links to the source and destination airports of flights, showing which airports have had flights depart from or arrive at them.

Each row represents a flight, listing the airline, flight number, and source and destination airports. It links to the airports for more details on where the flight departs and lands. The airlines table references it to show which flights are operated by each carrier.
Each row represents a county, recording its ID, name, population, and ZIP code. It links to the district in an election, helping match counties to their respective voting districts.
Each row represents a political party in an election year. It records the party name and details of its candidates for governor, lieutenant governor, comptroller, attorney general, and U.S. Senate.

Each row represents an election for a political position. It records the counties involved, the district, the delegate, the political party, when the delegate was first elected, and the committee overseeing the election. It links to counties and parties, providing context about where and under what conditions the election took place.

Each row represents a manufacturer, including its code, name, headquarters location, founder, and annual revenue. It links to the products table, showing which manufacturers produce each item and their financial details.
Each row represents a product made by the manufactory, listing its code, name, price, and manufacturer. It links to the manufacturer table to show which products are made by each company.

Each row represents a person involved in debates, recording their district, name, political party, and age. It links to the affirmative and negative sides of debates, showing which people support each side.
Each row represents a debate event, recording its ID, date, venue, and number of attendees. It links to the people who participated in the debate, showing which debates each person attended.

Each row represents a participant in a debate, noting whether they are on the affirmative or negative side. It links to the debate and the person involved, showing who debated what and their position.
Each row represents a person, with their name, age, city, gender, and job. It links to other people who are friends of this person and to the friends of those people.

Each row records a friendship between two people. It lists one person's name, their friend's name, and the year they became friends. It links to the person table twice, once for each name involved in the friendship.
Each row represents a type of service provided by local governments in Alabama. It records the service's unique identifier and its type. It links to events that record when these services are used.

Each row represents a participant in local government activities, identified by a unique ID. It includes the type of participant and additional details about them. It connects to events where the participant took part.

Each row represents an event, identified by a unique ID. It includes details of the event and its associated service. It links to participants in events and services, showing which events are related to specific services and who attended them.
Each row records a participant in an event. It links to the event and the participant, allowing you to see who attended which events.
Each row represents a mountain, recording its ID, name, height, prominence, range, and the country it is located in. It links to the climbers who have ascended it.

Each row represents a climber, recording their unique identifier, name, country, and performance metrics like time and points. It links to the mountain they climbed, showing which mountains each climber has ascended.
Each row represents an author or tutor in e-learning courses. It includes their login details, full names, gender and address. Courses refer to it to identify who teaches them.

Each row represents a student enrolled in e-learning courses. It records the student's registration date, login details, and full name. It links to course enrolments, showing which courses each student is taking.
Each row represents a subject or course category. It records the unique identifier and the name of the subject. Courses reference this table to categorize their offerings.

Each row represents a course offered in the e-learning system. It includes the course ID, author ID, subject ID, name and description. It links to the authors who created the courses and to the subjects they belong to. Joining it with student_course_enrolment shows which students are enrolled in each course.
Each row records a student's enrolment in an e-learning course, including the dates they enrolled and completed. It links to the student and the course, and connects to tests taken by the student.
Each row records a test result for a student, noting the date the test was taken and its outcome. It links to the student's course enrolment, showing which tests each student has completed.
Each row represents a scientist identified by their social security number. It records the scientist's full name. It links to other tables that assign tasks or projects to scientists.

Each row represents a project, identified by a code. It records the project's name and the number of hours allocated to it. The table links to the assignedto table, allowing tracking of which scientists are working on each project.
Each row records a scientist and the project they are assigned to. It links to the scientist's social security number and the project code, showing which scientists work on which projects.
Each row represents a ship's captain, recording their ID, name, age, the ship they command and their rank. It links to the ship to identify which vessel each captain commands.
Each row represents a ship, identified by its ID. It records the ship's name, type, year it was built, class and flag (country of registration). It links to the captain assigned to each ship.
Each row represents a film or television festival, including its name, the chairperson's name, location, year it was held, and number of attendees. It links to nominations related to that festival.

Each row represents an artistic work (such as a film or book) that has received an award. It records the work's ID, its type and its name. It links to nominations, showing which works were nominated for awards.

Each row is a nomination for an entertainment award. It records the artwork nominated, the festival it was submitted to, and whether it won. It links to the artwork and festival details, providing context about which works were nominated where.
Each row represents a type of allergy, recording the specific allergy and its general category. It links to the `has_allergy` table to show which patients have each type of allergy.
Each row indicates that a student has an allergy. It links to the student and the specific type of allergy they have, but does not provide details about the allergy itself.
Each row represents a student, recording their ID, last name, first name, age, gender, major, advisor and city code. It links to the table that records allergies for students.
Each row represents an actor, with their unique ID, gender, name, nationality, birth city, and birth year recorded. It links to the cast table to show which movies they have acted in.

Each row represents a copyright entry, identified by an ID. It includes the MSID and CID. It connects to other tables like cast, classification, and directed_by, linking these entries back to their respective data.

Each row represents a casting entry, listing an actor's role in a movie. It includes the actor's ID, the movie's ID and the role played. It links to the actor and the movie, connecting performances to performers.
Each row represents a movie genre, identified by a unique code. It records the genre name. The table is referenced to classify movies by their genres.
Each row is a film classification, identified by an ID. It links to the film's MSID and its genre GID, providing categorization details for each movie.
Each row represents a production company, identified by an ID. It records the company's name and its country of origin.

Each row represents a director, recording their unique identifier, gender, name, nationality, birth city, and birth year. It links to the movies they directed, allowing you to find which films each director has worked on.

Each row represents a film producer, recording their ID, gender, name, nationality, birth city, and birth year. It links to the movies they produced, allowing you to find which films were made by each producer.
Each row records a film director and the movies they directed. It links to movie metadata (msid) and directors (did). Joining it allows finding which directors made specific films.
Each row is a movie keyword, identified by an ID. It records the actual keyword used to describe movies. This table has no direct links or references to other tables.

Each row records a production relationship, identifying the unique ID, movie ID, and producer ID. It links to the copyright information and the producer details, showing which producers are associated with each movie.
Each row is a movie, with its ID, title, release year, alternative title and budget. It provides details about individual films without linking to other tables.
Each row is a tag assigned to a media item, identified by its ID. It records the media's ID and a keyword ID (kid). It links to the media's copyright record.
Each row represents a TV series, including its unique ID, title, release year, number of seasons and episodes. It also notes any alternative titles and the budget.

Each row represents a writer, including their unique identifier, gender, name, nationality, number of episodes they wrote, and their birth city and year. It links to the written_by table, which records the writers of specific episodes.
Each row records a movie-writer relationship, linking movies to their writers. It uses IDs from the copyright and writer tables. Joining it allows finding which writers contributed to which movies.
Each row is a discount coupon, recording its unique ID, the date it was issued, and the discount amount. It links to customers who use these coupons for hiring products.

Each row represents a customer who hires products. It includes the customer's name, gender, and dates they became and last hired products. A coupon ID indicates if they have a discount. It links to discounts and transactions related to the customer.

Each row is a product hire booking, recording details like start and end dates, status, and financial information such as amounts payable and refunds. It links to the customer who made the booking and the products hired. Joining it allows viewing payment records, products booked, and availability updates.
Each row represents a product available for hire, including its type, daily hire cost, name and description. It links to records of which products were booked and to availability views.

Each row records a payment made for a product hire, including the booking ID, customer ID, type of payment, and amounts due and paid. It links to the booking and customer details, showing payments related to specific hires.

Each row records a product booked for hire, noting whether it was returned and if late. It includes the number of items booked and the total amount. It links to the bookings table and the products for hire, showing which products were hired and their details.
Each row shows the availability of a product for hire on a specific date. It records whether the product is available and links to the product and its booking information.
Each row represents a poll result for a candidate, including their support rate and other opinion metrics. It links to the person being polled.
Each row represents a person, recording their ID, gender, name, date of birth, height, and weight. It is linked to the candidate table, providing details about individuals who are candidates.
Each row is an album, identified by its ID. It records the album's title and the artist who performed it. It links to the artist and is linked from the tracks that belong to the album.
Each row represents an artist. It records the artist's unique ID and name. Albums link to it to identify their artists.
Each row represents a customer, including their name, address, and contact information. It links to the support representative who assists them. Invoices refer to it to identify the customer.

Each row represents an employee, including their name, job title, contact details and employment history. It links to the manager who reports to this employee. Customers are linked through the supportrepid field, showing which employee supports them.
Each row represents a music genre, identified by an ID and named. It links to tracks to categorize them by genre.

Each row is an invoice for a music purchase or subscription. It records the invoice ID, date, and billing address details along with the total amount paid. It links to the customer who made the purchase and to the items included in the invoice.

Each row is a line item from an invoice, detailing a song purchase. It records the invoice ID, track ID, unit price, and quantity. It links to the invoice and the track, showing which songs were bought and for how much on each invoice.
Each row is a media type (format) of music, identified by an ID. It records the name of the format, such as "MPEG audio file". Tracks refer to it to say what format their content is in.
Each row is a playlist (a collection of songs). It records the playlist's unique ID and its name. It links to the playlisttrack table, which connects playlists to individual songs.
Each row records a track on a playlist. It links to the playlist and to the track, showing which tracks are included in each playlist.

Each row is a music track, including its name, album, media type, genre, composer, length in milliseconds, size in bytes, and price. It links to the album, media type, and genre, and connects to invoices and playlists that reference tracks.

Each row represents a flight route between two airports operated by an airline. It records the source and destination airports, the airline, and whether it's a code share. It links to the airports and the airline involved in the route.

Each row represents an airport, including its ID, name, city, country, and coordinates. It also includes the IATA and ICAO codes used to identify it in flight schedules. This table is referenced by the routes table to determine destination and source airports.

Each row represents an airline, including its ID, name, IATA and ICAO codes, call sign, country of origin, and whether it is currently active. It links to the routes table, allowing you to see which airlines operate on specific flight routes.
Each row represents a student, recording their ID, first and last names, age, gender, major, advisor, and the city code. It links to which students have pets.
Each row records that a student owns a pet. It links to the student and the pet, showing which students have which pets.
Each row represents a pet, recording its ID, type, age, and weight. It links to the table that tracks which pets belong to which owners.

Each row represents a student living in dorm 1. It includes the student's name, age, gender, major, and advisor. It links to the city code for the student's home city and is referenced by another table that records where students live.
Each row represents a dormitory (a living area for students) and includes its ID, name, capacity and gender restriction. It is referenced by tables that link amenities and student residences to it.
Each row describes a dormitory amenity (a facility or service) and its name. It links to the rooms that have these amenities, showing which facilities are available in each dorm room.
Each row records which amenities are available in a dorm. It links to the dorm and the specific amenity, showing what facilities each dorm has.
Each row records a student living in a specific room of the dorm. It links to the student and the dorm, showing which students reside in which rooms.

Each row represents an issue of a journal, noting the publication date, theme, and sales figures. It links to the journal committee table, allowing tracking of which issues were discussed or approved by the committee.
Each row represents an editor, recording their ID, name, and age. It links to the journal committee table, showing which editors are part of the committee.
Each row records an editor's role on a journal committee, noting the work type. It links to editors and journals, showing which editors serve on which committees and what their roles are.
Each row represents a flight, including its number, origin, destination, distance, and departure and arrival dates. It also records the flight's price and links to the aircraft that operates it.

Each row represents an aircraft, identified by its airline ID. It records the aircraft's name and the maximum distance it can fly. It links to flights operated by the aircraft and to certificates related to it.
Each row represents an employee, with their ID, name, and salary. It links to the certificate table, showing which certificates an employee holds.

Each row is a certificate held by an employee, identified by their employee ID and the airline ID. It links to the employee and the aircraft, recording which employees are certified for which aircraft.

Each row is a medicine, identified by an ID. It records the medicine's name, its trade name and whether it is FDA-approved. The table connects to the interaction table, linking medicines to their enzyme interactions.

Each row describes an enzyme, including its name, location in the body, and related genetic information. It links to the medicine-enzyme interaction table, providing details on which medicines interact with each enzyme.

Each row describes an interaction between a medicine and an enzyme. It records the enzyme's ID, the medicine's ID, and the type of interaction. It links to the enzyme and medicine tables, providing details on how medicines interact with specific enzymes.
Each row represents a customer, holding their basic details. It links to records of events related to the customer but does not link to other tables directly.

Each row represents a property and includes its ID, type code, address, and additional details. It links to records of residents who live there and notes related to customers or events at the property.

Each row represents a resident and their association with a property. It records the date they moved in, when they moved out, and any other details. It links to services related to residents and properties, and to events and notes involving residents.

Each row represents an organization, including its ID and a description. It links to other organizations indicating a hierarchical relationship and is referenced by tables tracking services and physical things managed by these organizations.

Each row represents a local government service, identified by its ID. It includes the type of service and more detailed information about it. It links to the organization that provides the service and is linked from tables tracking services provided to residents.

Each row records a service provided to a resident (such as garbage collection or snow removal). It includes the resident's ID, the service ID, dates of request and provision, and other details. It links to the resident and their property, showing when they moved in and which property is involved.

Each row represents a thing (an item or service) provided by an organization. It records the type of thing, its service type and additional details. It links to timed status updates, organizational information, and locations where the things are found or used.

Each row records an event in a customer's relationship with local government, such as moving into a property. It includes the date moved in, the customer ID, property ID, resident ID, and thing ID. It links to customers, residents, properties, and things, providing context for events like moves or changes.

Each row contains notes about an event related to a customer, such as moving into a property. It records the event's ID, the service type, and details like the resident and property involved. It links to events, residents, and properties, providing context for each note.
Each row records the status of a thing at a specific date. It includes the thing's ID, the date, and its status code. It links to the things table, providing historical status updates for each item.
Each row records the location of a thing at a specific date and time, identified by a unique thing ID. It links to the table that describes the things being tracked.
Each row represents a train, recording its unique ID, train number, name, starting point, ending point, scheduled time and interval between departures. It links to the routes that define its journey.

Each row represents a weather monitoring station, identified by an ID. It records the station's network name, the services it provides and the local authority it belongs to. It is linked to routes and weekly weather data, allowing connections to track service areas and weather patterns.
Each row records a train's route, linking a train to the stations it stops at. It shows which stations are part of a train's journey.

Each row represents the weather conditions for a specific day of the week at a weather station. It records the high and low temperatures, precipitation amount, and wind speed in miles per hour. It links to the station that monitors the weather.
Each row represents a shop member, recording their unique ID, card number, name, hometown, and membership level. It links to the branch where the member registered and to their purchases.

Each row represents a shop branch, including its name, opening year, and address. It records the membership amount required for that branch. It connects to the register of members associated with each branch and to purchase records linked to branches.
Each row records a member's registration at a store branch, noting the year they joined. It links to members and branches, showing which members belong to which branches and when.

Each row records a member's total purchase amount at a store for a given year. It includes the member ID, branch ID, and total weight of purchases in pounds. It links to members and branches, showing each member's spending across different stores over time.
Each row is an address, recording the line number or building name, city, zip code, state or province, and country. It links to staff and customer records, showing where they are based or live.

Each row represents a staff member at the driving school, including their nickname and full name. It records when they started and left the staff. The address is linked through staff_address_id. Lessons connect to this table to show which instructor taught each lesson.

Each row represents a vehicle used for driving lessons. It records the vehicle's identification and its details, such as make and model. It links to the lessons table, showing which vehicles were used in each lesson.

Each row represents a customer of the driving school, including their name, date of birth, contact details and status. It records when they became a customer and any outstanding fees. It links to their address and payments, and connects to their lesson bookings.

Each row records a payment made by a customer. It includes the date and time of the payment, the payment method used, and the amount paid. It links to the customer who made the payment, providing details on their payments over time.

Each row represents a driving lesson, recording the lesson's status, the instructor and vehicle used, the date and time, and the cost. It links to the customer taking the lesson, the instructor providing it, and the vehicle used.

Each row represents a stadium where concerts are held. It records the stadium's ID, location, name, and seating capacity. It also tracks the highest, lowest, and average attendance figures. This table is referenced by the concert table to link concerts to their venues.

Each row represents a singer, including their unique ID, name, country of origin, and details like gender and age. It links to the concerts they perform in, allowing you to see which singers are part of specific performances.
Each row represents a concert, including its name, theme, the stadium where it was held and the year. It links to the stadium and connects to singers performing at the concert.
Each row records a singer performing at a concert. It links to the concert and the singer, showing which singers performed in each concert.

Each row is a song identified by a unique ID. It records the song's title. It links to other tables that describe which instruments play the song, performances of it, its use in tracks, and the vocal parts.
Each row represents an album, with its ID, title, release year, record label, and type of album. It links to the tracks that belong to it, allowing you to see which songs are on each album.
Each row represents a band member, recording their first and last names. It links to other tables that list the instruments they play, their performances, and their roles as vocalists.

Each row lists the instruments used in a song, identified by its ID. It records which instrument was played and by which band member. It links to the songs table and to the band members who played the instruments.
Each row represents a band member's role in a performance, noting the song being performed and the band member's stage position. It links to the song and the band member.
Each row is a track in an album, listing the song's position and its ID. It links to the album and the song, showing which songs are on each album.
Each row represents a vocalist in a song, noting the singer's name and their role. It links to the song and the band member involved, connecting vocals data to songs and band members.

Each row represents a sports club, recording its ID, name, region, and the year it started. It connects to other tables like player, club ranking, and competition results, linking clubs in various contexts such as players' affiliations, rankings, and competition outcomes.

Each row ranks a sports club based on their medal count. It records the club's ID, the number of gold, silver, and bronze medals, and the total. It links to the club table for more details about each club.
Each row represents a player in the sports competition, recording their name, position, and statistics like appearances, tries, goals, and total points. It links to the player's club.
Each row represents a sports competition, including its ID, year, type, and the country it was held in. It links to the results of the competition, showing which competitions have recorded results.

Each row records the result of a sports competition between two clubs, noting which clubs played and their score. It links to the competition and the clubs involved, showing which competitions each club participated in.

Each row represents a railway locomotive, recording its unique identifier, name, builder, year built, wheel configuration, and location. It links to management records and is linked from trains that use it.

Each row represents a train, identified by its ID. It records the train number, name, departure station, arrival time and the railway company it belongs to. It links to the railway company that operates the train.
Each row represents a railway manager, including their ID, name, country of work, start year, age, and job level. It links to the table that records railway management relationships.

Each row represents a railway managed by a specific manager since a certain year. It records the railway's ID, the manager's ID and the start year of their management. It links to the railway and manager tables, allowing you to see which railways are managed by whom and when.
Each row represents a hotel room, detailing its ID, name, number of beds, bed type, maximum occupancy, base price, and decor. It links to the reservations table to show which rooms are booked.

Each row represents a hotel reservation. It records the reservation code, check-in and check-out dates, room number, rate, guest names, and number of adults and kids. It links to the specific room booked, allowing details about which rooms are reserved on what dates.
Each row represents a museum, including its ID, name, number of staff, and year it opened. It links to the visit table, showing which museums visitors have visited.
Each row represents a museum visitor, recording their unique ID, name, membership level, and age. It links to the visits table to track which exhibits or events they attended.
Each row represents a visit to a museum, recording the number of tickets purchased and the total amount spent. It links to the museum and the visitor, providing details about each visit.

Each row describes a web client accelerator, noting its ID, name, operating system, the client it accelerates, and the type of connection. It links to compatible browsers that can use the accelerator.
Each row represents a web browser, identified by an ID. It records the browser's name and its market share. It links to the browsers that are compatible with an accelerator.
Each row records which browsers are compatible with a specific web client accelerator, noting the year they became compatible. It links to the accelerator and the browser, showing their relationship.

Each row records an appearance of a player in an All-Star game, including the year, team and league. It notes whether the player started. It links to the player's details but does not link back or reference other tables directly.

Each row shows a player's appearances for a team in a given year. It records the number of games played in various positions and as a batter or defender. It links to the team and player, providing details on their playing time.
Each row records a manager's award, including the player ID, award ID, year, and whether it was a tie. It links to the player who received the award but has no primary key.

Each row records an award won by a baseball player, including the player's ID, the award ID, the year it was given, and if it was tied. It links to the player who received the award but does not directly connect to other tables.
Each row records a vote for a manager award, including the year, league, and points earned. It does not have a primary key or link to other tables.
Each row records a vote for a player in an annual award. It includes the award ID, year, league, player voted for, points won and maximum possible points. It links to the player receiving votes.

Each row shows a player's batting statistics for a specific year and stint. It records the number of games played, at-bats, runs, hits, doubles, triples, home runs, RBIs, stolen bases, walks, strikeouts, and other relevant stats. It links to the player's record in the player table.

Each row shows a player's batting statistics during the postseason for a specific year and round. It records games played, at-bats, runs, hits, home runs, and other key stats. It links to the player and team involved, allowing you to see each player’s performance across different teams and years.

Each row records a player's college attendance, noting the player and college IDs along with the year. It links to the player and college tables, providing details on which players attended which colleges and when.

Each row records a fielding performance for a player in a specific year and stint. It includes details like games played, outs, putouts, assists, errors, double plays, and defensive runs saved. It links to the player who performed the fielding.

Each row records an outfielder's fielding statistics for a season. It includes the number of games played in left field (glf), centre field (gcf), and right field (grf). It links to the player who made these plays.

Each row records a player's fielding statistics for a postseason game. It includes the year, team, league, position, games played, innings, putouts, assists, errors, double plays, triples, passed balls, stolen bases and caught stealing. It links to the player who recorded these stats.

Each row represents a year's vote for a baseball player to the Hall of Fame. It records who voted, the number of ballots cast, votes received, whether the player was inducted, the category, and any notes on votes needed. It links to the player's details.

Each row represents a home game played by a baseball team in a specific year. It records the league, team, ballpark, span of dates for the season, number of games, openings, and attendance. It links to the team and ballpark information.

Each row represents a manager's performance for a season. It records the player ID, year, team, league, number of games managed, wins, losses, and rank. It links to the team table to identify the specific team.
Each row represents a manager's performance for a season half, recording the number of games played (g), wins (w), losses (l), and ranking. It links to the team managed.

Each row represents a baseball player, including their full name, birth and death details, physical attributes, and career statistics. It links to other tables that record the player's achievements and positions in various awards and statistics.
Each row represents a baseball stadium, recording its ID, name, and location details like city, state, and country. It links to the home games played there.

Each row represents a pitching performance for a player in a specific year and stint. It records statistics like wins, losses, games started, innings pitched, hits allowed, earned runs, home runs, walks, strikeouts, and more. It links to the player, team, and league but does not have a primary key.

Each row records a pitcher's performance in postseason games, including wins, losses, innings pitched, and statistics like hits, runs, and strikeouts. It does not link to or reference any other table directly.
Each row records a baseball player's salary for a specific year, including the team and league. It links to no other tables and is not referenced by any others.
Each row represents a college, recording its full name, city, state, and country. It links to the player_college table to show which players attended each college.
Each row records a postseason series in baseball, including the winning and losing teams, their leagues, and the number of wins, losses, and ties. It does not link to or reference any other table.

Each row represents a baseball team's performance in a specific year, including wins, losses, and various statistics like runs scored and earned run average. It does not have a primary key and is referenced by other tables tracking appearances, batting, home games, managers, and more.
Each row represents a baseball franchise, noting its name and whether it is still active. It also indicates the team's association with a North American league.
Each row represents a team's performance in one half of a baseball season. It includes the year, league, team identifier, division, win status, rank, games played, wins and losses.
Each row represents an architect, recording their unique ID, name, nationality, and gender. It links to the bridges and mills they designed.
Each row represents a bridge, including its unique identifier, name, location, and lengths in both meters and feet. It links to the architect who designed the bridge.
Each row represents a mill, identified by its unique ID. It records details such as the location, name, type of mill and the year it was built. It links to the architect who designed the mill.

Each row represents a CSU campus, including its name, location, county, and the year data was recorded. It links to other tables like fees, degrees, and enrollments, allowing connections between campus-specific information and broader educational metrics.

Each row records the campus fee for a specific campus and year. It includes the campus name, the year, and the associated fee amount. It links to the campuses table to identify the campus and to the years used in degree programs.

Each row represents the number of degrees awarded in a specific year at a particular campus. It records the year, campus, and total degrees awarded. It links to other tables on the year to connect data about degree programs across different campuses and years.

Each row shows the number of undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in a specific discipline at a campus for a given year. It links to campuses and degrees, providing context about where and when these enrollments occurred.

Each row shows the total enrollment and full-time equivalent students for a campus in a specific year. It links to campuses and degrees, allowing queries about student numbers across years and locations.

Each row represents a faculty member at a specific campus and academic year. It records the campus, year, and name of the faculty member. It links to the campuses table for the location and to the degrees table for the academic period.
Each row represents a customer, recording their ID, name, and additional details. It links to the orders table, showing which orders are placed by each customer.
Each row is an invoice, recording the invoice number, date, and details of a shipment. It links to shipments that are billed by this invoice.

Each row represents an order placed by a customer. It records the order's ID, status, placement date, and details. It links to the customer who placed it and connects to related order items and shipments.
Each row represents a product available for sale. It records the product's ID, name, and additional details. It links to the order items that reference it, showing which products are in orders.
Each row represents an item in an order, detailing which product is ordered and its status. It links to the product and the order, and connects to shipments that track delivery of these items.

Each row represents a shipment (a delivery of ordered items). It records the shipment ID, order ID, invoice number, tracking number and date. It links to the order and invoice, and connects to the items shipped in the shipment.
Each row records an item in a shipment, linking the shipment to its individual items. It connects to the shipment and the specific order items it contains.

Each row represents a customer. It contains details about the customer, such as their name and contact information. It is linked to the policies held by that customer, so joining it provides policy information for each customer.

Each row represents an insurance policy held by a customer. It records the policy ID, the customer's ID, the type of policy, and its start and end dates. It links to the customer who holds the policy and is linked from claims to determine which policies are associated with specific claims.

Each row represents an insurance claim, recording the claim ID, the policy it relates to, and the dates and amounts for both the claimed and settled values. It links to the policy and connects to the settlements table.
Each row is a settlement for an insurance claim, recording the date and amount of both the claim and its resolution. It links to the claim details and connects to the payments table.

Each row records a payment made for an insurance policy settlement. It includes the payment method, date, and amount. It links to the settlement it relates to, providing details of how and when payments were made.

Each row represents a gas company, including its rank, name, headquarters, main industry, and financial metrics like sales, profits, assets, and market value. It links to the stations operated by each company.

Each row represents a gas station, including its ID, year it opened, location, and names of the manager and vice manager. It links to and from the station_company table, recording company-wide information about each station.

Each row represents a gas station's ranking with a company for a given year. It records the station ID, company ID and the rank achieved. It links to the gas station and the company, showing which stations each company manages and their performance rankings.
Each row is an address, recording the line number and name of a building, town or city, ZIP or postcode, state or province, and country. It links to parties that have this address.

Each row represents a government service, identified by a unique ID. It includes the service type code, name and description. It is linked to related forms and parties using its ID, allowing details of available services to be matched with user requests and associated forms.

Each row is a government form, identified by its ID. It records the form type, associated service, number, name and description. It links to the service for which the form is used and connects to forms linked to parties in another table.

Each row represents an individual (a person) in the e-government system. It includes their first name, middle name, phone number, email, address, and last name. It links to where this individual is contacted within organizations and is referenced from those contact records.
Each row represents a government organization, recording its ID, formation date, name and UK VAT number. It links to the individuals associated with it, showing who works for each organization.

Each row represents a government party (such as an individual or organization) and includes their contact information like phone number and email. It links to additional addresses and forms, and connects to services where the party is the customer.

Each row records an individual's contact with a government organization, noting the dates when the contact began and ended. It links to the individual and the organization involved, allowing connections between people and departments.

Each row records an address associated with a government party, noting when the address began and ended. It links to the party and the specific address, allowing connections between parties and their locations over time.

Each row represents a government form submitted by a party. It records the party's ID, the form's ID, when completion started, the status of the form and when it was fully completed. It links to parties and forms, connecting who submitted which documents and their statuses.

Each row represents a booking for a government service. It records the booking ID, customer ID, service ID and the dates of both the booking and the service. It links to the customer and the service provided.
Each row represents a bus driver, recording their ID, name, employment status, home city, and age. It links to the school bus table to identify which buses are driven by each driver.

Each row represents a school, identified by its ID. It records the grade level, name, location and type of the school. The table connects to itself through the school_id, allowing relationships between schools and their buses.

Each row represents a school bus and its driver. It records the school the bus serves, the driver's ID, how many years the driver has worked, and if they are full-time. It links to the school and the driver, connecting buses to their assigned schools and drivers.

Each row represents a machine repair record. It includes the repair ID, the machine's name or model, the launch date of the machine, and any additional notes. It links to repair assignments, showing which repairs were assigned to technicians.
Each row represents a machine, recording its ID, manufacturing year, class, assigned maintenance team, series, and quality ranking. It links to the repairs assigned to it.

Each row represents a technician who repairs machines, including their name, team, when they started, and their current age. It links to the repair assignment table, showing which technicians are assigned to specific repairs.

Each row is a repair assignment, indicating which technician is assigned to fix a specific machine. It records the technician's ID, the repair ID, and the machine's ID. It links to technicians, repairs, and machines, allowing you to see which techs are assigned to which repairs for which machines.
Each row represents an artist, recording their ID, name, country of origin, year they joined the gallery, and their current age. It links to exhibitions where the artist's work is displayed.

Each row represents an exhibition, including its year, theme, and the artist. It records the ticket price and links to the artist responsible for the exhibition. Joining it with exhibition_record provides details of each exhibition's visitor count.

Each row records an exhibition, noting its ID and the date it took place. It also tracks how many people attended. It links to the exhibition table for more details and is referenced by it to show which exhibitions have records of attendance.
Each row represents a film, including its ID, title, studio, director and total box office earnings. It links to the film market estimation table for revenue forecasts.

Each row represents a film market in a country, identified by its ID. It records the country and the number of cities in that market. It is linked to estimates of a film's performance in those markets.

Each row estimates a film's potential box office performance. It records the low and high estimate, the film it applies to, the type of estimate, the relevant market, and the year. It links to films and markets, allowing you to see how different factors affect estimated earnings.
Each row represents a region, identified by its ID. It records the region's name and other details like date, label, format and catalogue information. It links to parties held in that region.

Each row represents a political party and records its name, the minister it was responsible to, when it took and left office, and the region it served. It links to the region and connects to members of parliament and party events involving the party.

Each row represents a political member, including their ID, name, the party they belong to, and whether they are currently in office. It links to the party table, providing details of which party each member is associated with. Joining it allows identifying key members responsible for organizing events.
Each row represents a party event, including its unique identifier and name. It records the party organizing the event and the member in charge. It links to the party and the responsible member.

Each row represents a physician (a medical doctor) with their employee ID, name, position, and Social Security Number.
