Each row represents a staff member in the insurance and eClaims system. It contains their identification number and detailed information. It links to documents created by the staff and to processing tasks assigned to them.

Each row represents an insurance policy held by a customer. It records the policy's ID, the customer ID, type of policy, start and end dates. It links to the customer who holds the policy and connects to claims related to it.

Each row is a claim header representing an insurance claim. It records the claim's status, type, policy ID, dates of submission and settlement, and amounts claimed and paid. It links to the policy associated with the claim and connects to documents and processing details related to it.

Each row is a document related to an insurance claim, including its type and the staff member who created it. It records the claim ID, the document type code, the creator's ID, and the creation date. It links to the claim header and the staff member who created the document.

Each row represents a stage in the claims processing workflow. It records the ID of the current and next stages, along with the status name and description. It links to the claims_processing table to track the progress of individual claims through these stages.

Each row represents a step in the processing of an insurance claim. It records the claim's ID, its outcome code and the stage it is at, along with the staff member handling it. It links to the claim header, the processing stage, and the staff member involved.

Each row represents a class (a course section) with its code, course it belongs to, section number, time, room, and the professor's employee number. It links to the course and professor tables, allowing you to find which courses are offered in specific sections and times, and who teaches them. Students enroll in these classes.

Each row represents a course offered at the college, identified by a code. It includes the department code, a description of the course and its credit value. It links to the department that offers the course and is referenced by classes that schedule it.

Each row represents a college department, including its code, name, and address. It also lists the number of employees and their extension. It links to employees, courses, professors, and students associated with the department.

Each row represents an employee, including their name, initial, job code, hire date, and date of birth. It links to classes taught by professors, departments they belong to, and their role as a professor.
Each row records a student's enrollment in a class, noting the class code and the student's number. It links to the class and the student, connecting enrollments to specific classes and students.

Each row represents a professor and includes their employee number, department code, office location, phone extension, and highest degree. It links to the employee and department tables, providing details about professors' roles and affiliations.

Each row represents a student, including their name, date of birth, class hours, GPA, transfer status, department code, and phone number. It links to the department for more details on the student's program and is referenced by enrollment records to track courses taken.
Each row is a record of a customer in the local government's master database. It contains detailed information about the customer. It links to other records that reference this customer.

Each row is a cross-reference in the customer master index, linking different identifiers for the same customer across various systems. It records the unique reference ID, the master customer ID, and the source system code. It connects to other tables like council tax, business rates, benefits overpayments, parking fines, rent arrears, and electoral register, allowing these records to be linked back to a single customer.

Each row represents a council tax record, identified by a unique council tax ID. It includes a cross-reference ID for linking to other systems. It connects to records of overpayments, parking fines, and rent arrears, helping to track financial issues related to council tax.
Each row represents a business rate, identified by a unique ID. It includes a cross-reference ID linking to additional details in another table.

Each row records an overpayment of benefits for a council tax payer. It links the overpayment to the council tax ID and a cross-reference ID, allowing connections to related data about the taxpayer and the overpayment details.

Each row represents a parking fine issued to a resident. It records the council tax ID of the person fined and an additional cross-reference ID. It links to the council tax record and related cross-references, providing more details about the fine.
Each row records rent arrears for a property, identified by the council tax ID. It links to additional reference information via the CMI cross-reference ID.

Each row represents a registered voter in the electoral register. It includes an identifier for the voter and a cross-reference ID linking to additional data. It connects to the CMI cross-references table for more details.

Each row represents a published edition of a book, including its unique identifier, the book it relates to, the publisher, and the publication date and price. It links back to the book table to identify which book is being published.
Each row is a book, recording its ID, title, number of issues, and the writer's name. It links to publications that reference this book.
Each row represents a company region, identified by an ID and named. It links to the countries table, showing which regions contain each country.

Each row represents a country, identified by its ID and named. It includes the country's region ID. It links to the regions table, showing which region each country belongs to. Locations refer to it to specify a country.

Each row represents a department in the company, including its ID, name, manager's ID, and location ID. It links to the location table for the department’s physical address. Employees and job history records refer to it to show which department they belong to or worked in.

Each row represents a job title in the company, including its ID and minimum and maximum salary ranges. It links to employee records and job history to show which jobs employees have had and their salary details.

Each row represents an employee, including their name, contact details, hire date, job title, salary, manager and department. It links to the jobs table for job titles and to departments. Joining with job_history shows an employee's work history over time.

Each row records a job position an employee has held, including the start and end dates. It links to the employee, their job title, and the department they worked in. Joining it with other tables shows an employee's career history within different departments.

Each row represents a company location, including its street address, postal code, city, state or province, and the associated country. It links to the countries table for more details on the country. Departments refer to it to specify where they are located.

Each row represents a set of attributes for a soccer player, including ratings for various skills like passing, dribbling, and stamina. It also includes goalkeeper-specific attributes. It links to the player table using the player IDs, providing detailed skill assessments over time.
Each row shows the next auto-increment value for a table in the database. It records the name of the table and its current sequence number.
Each row represents a soccer player, including their ID, API identifiers, name, date of birth, height, and weight. It links to additional player attributes for more detailed information.

Each row represents a soccer league, identified by an ID and named. It records the league's country of origin using a country ID. It links to the country table for more details on where the league is based.
Each row represents a country. It records the country's unique identifier and its name. The table is referenced by the league table to specify which country a league or team belongs to.

Each row represents a soccer team, identified by an ID. It includes the team's long and short names, as well as API IDs for FIFA and another data source. It connects to a table with more detailed attributes about the team.

Each row represents a set of attributes for a soccer team, including their play style and defensive strategies. It records metrics like build-up play speed, chance creation passing, defence pressure, and more. It links to the team through its FIFA API ID and API ID, allowing comparisons across different sources.

Each row represents an actor, with their unique ID, first name, and last name. It also notes when the record was last updated. This table connects to the film_actor table, linking actors to films they appear in.

Each row is an address, recording the full address including secondary address details, district, associated city, and contact information like phone number. It links to the city and is linked from tables for customers, staff, and stores.
Each row is a movie category (like action, comedy). It records the category's ID and name. It links to films that belong to this category.

Each row is a city, identified by an ID and named in plain text. It includes the ID of the country where the city is located and when the record was last updated. It links to the country table, allowing you to find which countries have cities listed. Addresses refer to it to specify where they are located.
Each row represents a country, identified by its ID. It records the country's name and when the record was last updated. Cities link to it to specify which country they are in.

Each row represents a customer who has used the Sakila video rental system. It includes their name, email, address details, and status information like whether they are active. It links to the store where they made purchases and the address where they are registered. Joining this table allows finding which rentals or payments belong to each customer.

Each row is a movie (a film) in the Sakila database. It records details like title, description, release year, languages used, rental and replacement costs, length, and rating. It links to related tables for categories, languages, actors, and inventory.

Each row represents an actor in a film. It records the actor's ID, the film's ID, and when the record was last updated. It links to actors and films, allowing you to see which actors are in which movies.

Each row categorizes a film, linking it to its category. It records the film's ID and the last update date. It connects to films and categories, allowing you to see which films belong to each category.
Each row is a film entry with its title and a brief description. It links to the full film details table, providing basic information about each movie.

Each row represents a copy of a film available for rent in the store. It records the film's ID, the store's ID, and the last update date. It links to the film and the store, allowing you to see which films are stocked where. Rentals refer to it to track which films were rented out.
Each row represents a movie language, identified by an ID. It records the language's name and when its record was last updated. It links to films by their primary and original languages.

Each row is a payment made for a video rental. It records the amount paid, the date of payment, and which customer, staff member, and rental it relates to. It links to customers, staff, and rentals, showing who paid what, when, and for which rental.

Each row is a movie rental, recording when a customer rented an item from a store. It includes the rental date, return date and staff member who processed it. It links to the inventory item rented, the customer who rented it and the staff member. Payments are linked back to rentals to show how much was paid for each one.

Each row represents a staff member at the video store. It includes their name, address, email, active status, username and password. It links to the address and store, and is linked from tables for payments, rentals, and store managers.

Each row represents a store, identifying its unique ID and the staff member who manages it. It also records the address ID and when the record was last updated. This table connects to addresses for store locations and to staff and customers associated with each store.
Each row is a property feature type (like "balcony" or "garage"). It records the feature's code and its name. Other tables reference it to describe available features for properties.
Each row defines a type of real estate property, such as house or apartment. It records the property type code and its description. The properties table uses this to categorize listings.

Each row describes an additional feature available for a property, such as a garage or fireplace. It records the feature type code, name and a description. It links to the list of feature types and is linked from properties that have these features.

Each row represents a real estate property listed for sale or rent. It includes details like address, room count, prices from vendor and buyer, and various features of the property such as apartment, field, house, and other details. The table links to reference data for property types and is referenced by another table that lists additional features.
Each row describes an additional feature of a real estate property, such as a garage or pool. It links to the main property and to the available features list.

Each row represents a student, recording their ID, first and last names, age, gender, major, advisor, and the city code. It links to tables that show which minors are in which students' care and which courses the students are enrolled in.

Each row represents a faculty member (a teacher or professor) at the college. It includes their name, rank, contact information like phone and office details. It connects to records of courses they teach and departments they are part of.

Each row represents a college department, including its number, division, name, room, building and phone. It connects to tables for faculty members, courses offered, and students' minors, allowing details about departmental affiliations to be linked.

Each row records a faculty member's appointment to a department, noting the faculty ID, department number, and appointment type. It links to the faculty and department tables, showing which professors are assigned to which departments.

Each row represents a course offered at the college, including its ID, name, credit value, instructor, days of the week it meets, and hours. It links to the instructor's faculty ID and the department number, showing which faculty member teaches the course and which department it belongs to. Students are linked through to show who is enrolled in each course.
Each row records a student's minor (a secondary field of study). It links to the student and their chosen department. Joining it shows which students have declared minors in specific departments.

Each row records a student's enrollment in a course, including the student ID, course ID and grade received. It links to the student, course, and grade conversion tables to provide full details of enrollments.
Each row converts a letter grade to its corresponding grade point. It records the letter grade and the associated grade point. This table is referenced when converting grades in student enrollments.
Each row represents a course offering, including its start date and name. It links to the detailed arrangements for the course, allowing you to see when and where it is taught.
Each row represents a teacher, recording their ID, name, age, and hometown. It links to the course arrangement table, showing which courses each teacher is assigned to teach.
Each row arranges a course with its teacher and the grade level. It links to the course and teacher tables, showing which teachers teach which courses at what grade level.

Each row represents a roller coaster, including its unique identifier, name, park location, and details like length, height, speed, opening year, and current status. It links to the country where the park is located.
Each row represents a country, with its ID, name, population, area and official languages. It links to the roller coaster table to specify which countries have roller coasters.
Each row represents a product offered for delivery, including its ID, name, price, and description. It is referenced by tables that record products in regular and actual orders.

Each row is an address, recording the details of a delivery location including the street address, city, zip code, state or province, and country. It links to customers, delivery routes, and employee addresses, allowing these records to reference multiple locations.
Each row represents a customer, recording their name, contact information and when they started doing business. It links to the addresses associated with each customer and to their regular orders.

Each row represents a regular delivery order placed with a distributor. It records the order ID and the distributor's ID. It links to the distributor, allowing you to see which orders they handle. This table connects to details of the products in each order and to actual deliveries made.
Each row records a product in a regular delivery order. It links to the order and the product, showing which products are part of which orders.

Each row represents a completed delivery order. It records the order's status, its original order ID, and the date it was placed. It links to the regular order from which it originated and connects to the products delivered and deliveries made for this order.
Each row records a product included in an actual order. It links to the order and the product, showing which products were ordered.

Each row represents an address associated with a customer, noting the start and end dates of its validity. It links to the customer and the specific address details, allowing tracking of which addresses were used for deliveries during different periods.

Each row represents a delivery route, identified by a unique ID. It includes the route's name and any additional details about it. It connects to locations that specify where deliveries follow this route.

Each row represents a delivery location on a route, identified by a code. It records the location's address and its name. It links to the delivery route and the address, allowing you to find all locations on a route or deliveries made to a specific address.

Each row represents a delivery truck, recording its ID and licence number. It includes additional details about the truck. It links to the order deliveries table, allowing tracking of which trucks are used for specific orders.

Each row represents an employee who delivers customer orders. It includes the employee's ID, address ID, name, and phone number. The address ID links to the employee's address details. Joining this table with order deliveries shows which driver delivered each order.

Each row records a delivery, noting the location code, order ID, status, driver employee ID, truck ID, and delivery date. It links to delivery routes, orders, drivers, and trucks, providing details on each delivery.

Each row represents a stadium, recording its name and details like the number of home games played there, average and total attendance, and how full it is on average. It links to the game table, allowing connections between injuries that occurred in specific games and the stadiums where those games were held.

Each row represents a game played, recording the stadium, season, date, teams playing, final score and competition. It links to the stadium where the game was held. The table connects to records of injuries that occurred during the game.

Each row records an injury suffered by a player during a game. It includes details like the type of injury, how many matches the player missed, and the source of the information. It links to the game where the injury occurred.

Each row represents a school, including its name, location, mascot, enrollment, and IHSAA classification for football and overall. It links to the budget and endowment tables, allowing financial data and endowment information to be matched with schools.

Each row represents a school's budget for a fiscal year, recording the total budgeted amount and how much was actually invested. It links to the school it belongs to and shows the percentage of the budget that was invested.

Each row represents an endowment (a donation to a school). It records the endowment's unique ID, the school it benefits, the donor's name, and the amount donated. It links to the school receiving the donation.
Each row represents an author identified by a unique ID. It records the author's name. The table is referenced by papers to attribute them to authors.
Each row cites a paper and records its author's ID and name. It links to the papers that cite it, showing which authors referenced this work.
Each row represents a dataset, identified by its ID and name. It links to papers that use the dataset, allowing you to find which datasets are referenced in scholarly works.
Each row represents a scholarly journal, identified by its ID and name. It links to papers published in the journal, allowing you to find which articles belong to each journal.

Each row is a key phrase or keyword. It records the unique identifier and the text of the key phrase. It links to the paperkeyphrase table, which connects papers to their key phrases, allowing searches based on keywords.

Each row represents a scholarly paper, including its title, year of publication, and number of citations. It links to the venue where it was published, the journal if applicable, and the authors who wrote it. Joining with related tables provides details on citations, key phrases, datasets, and more.
Each row records a citation where one paper references another. It links to the citing and cited papers, showing which papers cite each other.

Each row links a paper to its key phrases, identified by the key phrase ID. It records which papers contain specific key phrases and what those phrases are. Joining it with other tables allows finding papers by their key phrases or key phrases by the papers they appear in.
Each row records a key phrase associated with a paper. It links to the paper and to the key phrase, helping to connect papers by their shared terms.

Each row records an authorship of a scholarly paper. It links to the paper and the author, showing which papers each author has written. Joining it with other tables can show detailed information about authors' publications.
Each row represents an area code and the state it is located in. It links to the state but not directly to any other table, so joining it helps identify states by their area codes.
Each row represents a contestant in a competition, with their assigned number and name. It links to the votes table to show which voters chose each contestant.

Each row represents a vote recorded for an election. It includes the voter's phone number, the state they are from, the contestant they voted for, and when the vote was cast. It links to the state and contestant tables, providing context about where and who the vote is for.
Each row represents a country, recording its ID, name, capital city, and official native language. It links to the match season table to specify which countries participate in the season.
Each row represents a team in the league, identified by a unique ID. It records the team's name. The table is referenced to link teams to matches and players.

Each row represents a player's position and performance in a specific match season. It includes details like the player, their position, country, team, draft pick number, and college. It links to the country and team tables, providing context about where the player is from and which team they play for.

Each row represents a player in the match season, recording their name, years played, total win/loss record, and separate records for singles and doubles matches. It also notes which team they played for.
Each row represents a customer account, recording the customer's ID and name. It links to both savings and checking accounts, showing which accounts belong to each customer.
Each row represents a customer's savings account, recording the account balance. It links to and from the accounts table, showing which accounts are savings accounts and their balances.
Each row represents a customer's checking account balance. It records the account balance for each customer. It links to the accounts table, showing which customers have checking accounts.

Each row represents a tennis player, recording their first name, last name, playing hand, birth date, and country. It links to match results showing wins and losses, and to rankings showing their performance.

Each row represents a tennis match, recording details like the best-of sets, scores, and player information. It links to the players table for both winners and losers, providing comprehensive match data.

Each row represents a player's ranking on a specific date. It includes the ranking position, total ranking points and number of tournaments played. It links to the player's details in the players table.

Each row represents a business listed on Yelp, including its name, address, city, latitude and longitude. It also records the number of reviews, whether it is open, its rating, and state. This table connects to other tables like categories, check-ins, neighborhoods, reviews, and tips through the business_id.
Each row is a category assigned to a business. It records the category name and links back to the business it applies to.
Each row represents a Yelp user, identified by a unique ID. It records the user's name. This table is linked to reviews and tips, which reference the user who wrote them.

Each row records a check-in count for a specific day at a Yelp business. It includes the number of times people checked in and the date. It links to the business to identify which establishment is being tracked.

Each row represents a neighbourhood and the businesses located within it. It records the neighbourhood's name and its association with specific business IDs. It links to the businesses in that neighbourhood, allowing you to find which businesses are in each area.
Each row is a customer review of a business. It includes the review ID, rating, text, and the year and month it was written. It links to the business being reviewed and the user who wrote the review.
Each row is a tip left by a Yelp user about a business. It records the text of the tip, how many likes it received, and when it was posted. It links to the business and the user who wrote the tip.

Each row represents a student, listing their last name, first name, grade level, and the classroom they are in. It links to teachers by the last name, showing which teacher is associated with each student.
Each row represents a teacher and includes their last name, first name, and the classroom they teach. It links to a list of students and is linked from that same list.

Each row represents a manufacturer, including its ID, year it opened, name, number of factories, and number of shops. It links to the furniture manufacture table, allowing details about furniture manufacturing by this company.
Each row represents a piece of furniture, recording its ID, name, number of components, and market value. It links to the manufacturer who produced it but does not directly reference other tables.

Each row represents a furniture item made by a manufacturer. It records the price of the furniture in dollars. It links to the manufacturer and the furniture, showing which manufacturers produce which items and their prices.
Each row represents an artist, identified by a unique ID and named by its sequential position. It is referenced by the albums table to link artists to their album creations.
Each row is a sequence value for an artist table, used to generate unique IDs. It records the name and the next sequence number.

Each row is an album held in the store, identified by a unique ID. It records the album's title and the artist who performed it. It links to the artist table and connects to the tracks that belong to this album.

Each row represents an employee, including their name, job title, and contact information. It records details like birth date, hire date, address, and phone number. Employees report to other employees, creating a hierarchy. Customers can be linked to an employee for support purposes.

Each row represents a customer of the store, including their name, address, and contact information. It also records which employee supports them. Invoices link to it to identify the customer who received an invoice.
Each row represents a genre of music. It records the genre's unique identifier and its name. The tracks table references it to categorize songs by their genre.

Each row is an invoice for a purchase, including the customer who bought it and the total amount. It records the invoice date and billing address details. It links to the customer and connects to the items included in the invoice.
Each row represents a type of media (like DVD or CD). It records the media type's ID and its name. Tracks refer to it to specify the type of each track in a media item.

Each row represents a music track, including its name, album, media type, genre, composer, length in milliseconds and price. It links to the album, media type, and genre tables, allowing details of each track's broader context. It is referenced by invoice lines and playlists, showing which tracks are sold or included in playlists.

Each row is a line item from an invoice, detailing a music track's sale. It records the track ID, unit price, and quantity sold. It links to the invoice and the track, providing a breakdown of each invoice.
Each row is a playlist, identified by an ID and named. It links to the tracks in the playlist but has no direct information about them.
Each row is a track in a playlist. It records the playlist and track IDs, linking to the playlist and the track itself.

Each row represents a train station, recording its name and annual entry-exit statistics. It includes the total number of passengers, location, main services offered, and number of platforms. This table is referenced by other tables to link back to specific stations.
Each row represents a train, with its unique identifier, name, scheduled time, and service type. It links to the train station table, showing which trains stop at each station.
Each row records a train's stop at a station. It links to the train and the station, showing which trains stop where. Joining it with other tables can show the schedule of each train.
Each row defines a user role, with a unique code and description. It links to the users table to show which roles are assigned to each user.
Each row represents a user in the system, including their unique ID, role, name, login, and password. It links to the roles table to define the user's permissions.

Each row defines a document structure (a template or format) and its parent structure. It records the structure's code, a description of what it is used for, and if it inherits from another structure. Documents refer to it to determine their format.

Each row represents a functional area (a category of documents) with a unique code and description. It may also have a parent code indicating its broader category. Documents reference it to show their areas of function.
Each row is an image stored in the system, with its alternative text description, file name, and URL. It links to sections of documents that use this image.

Each row represents a document, identified by its code. It records the document's structure code, type code, access count and name. It links to the document structures and sections that define its format, and is linked from tables showing which functional areas it relates to and what sections it contains.
Each row records the relationship between a document and its functional areas. It links to the document's code and the functional area's code, showing which areas are relevant to each document.

Each row represents a section within a document, identified by its sequence and code. It records the section's title and its position in the document. It links to images associated with the section and is linked from those images.

Each row links a document section to its associated image. It records the section ID and the image ID. It connects to the document sections and images tables, allowing you to see which images belong to each section of a document.
Each row represents a race circuit used in Formula 1, including its ID, name, location, country, and coordinates. It links to the races table, providing details about where each race is held.

Each row represents a Formula 1 race, including its unique identifier (raceid), year, round number, circuit name and date. It links to circuits for the track details and to other tables like results and standings for comprehensive race data.

Each row represents a Formula 1 driver, recording their ID, name, year number, constructor details, date of birth, nationality and URL. It links to tables that record race results, standings, qualifying positions, pit stops and lap times.
Each row represents a race season in Formula 1, identified by a unique ID. It records the race ID. It links to the results table, providing the race context for each result.
Each row represents a Formula 1 season, identified by the year. It records the points awarded in that season. It links to race results for that year.

Each row represents a constructor's (a racing team) standing, including their position, name, and nationality. It links to other tables that record race results, qualifying sessions, and detailed standings.

Each row shows a constructor's (team's) standing after a race, including points scored, position, and number of wins. It links to the race and the constructor, connecting results across multiple races.

Each row shows a driver's position and points after a race. It records the race, driver, constructor, fastest lap time, grid position, and other race results like laps completed and final status. It links to races, drivers, constructors, and race statuses.

Each row shows a driver's standing after a race, including points scored, race position, and whether they won. It links to the race and the driver involved, so you can see each driver’s performance in every race.

Each row represents a constructor's result in a qualifying session. It records the race, the constructor's ID, points scored and the status. It links to the race and the constructor, connecting qualifying results to their respective races and teams.

Each row represents a qualifying session for a Formula 1 circuit. It records the circuit ID, race reference, driver name, constructor location, country number, and position details like latitude, longitude, altitude, and URL. It links to races, drivers, and constructors, providing context about where and when each qualifying session took place.
Each row records a pit stop during a Formula 1 race, noting the driver, stop number, lap, time, and duration. It links to the race and the driver, providing details of each pit stop in every race.

Each row records a lap time for a driver in a Formula 1 race. It includes the lap number, driver's position, and time in milliseconds. It links to the race and the driver, providing detailed timing data per lap.
Each row represents a student, recording their ID, first and last names, age, gender, major, advisor, and the city code. It links to records of games played and sports information.
Each row represents a video game, identified by its ID. It records the game's name and type. It links to the players who have played it, allowing you to see which games users have enjoyed.
Each row records how many hours a student has played a particular game. It links to the student and the game, showing which students have played which games and for how long.

Each row records a student's participation in a sport, noting the sport name, hours practiced weekly, number of games played, and whether they are on a scholarship. It links to the student who plays the sport.

Each row represents a bank branch, including its name, number of customers, and location details like city and state. It links to the customers and loans associated with that branch, allowing queries about branch-specific data.

Each row represents a customer and includes their name, account type, balance, number of loans, credit score, the branch they are associated with, and their state. It links to the branch table, providing details about which branch serves the customer. Loans are linked back to customers through cust_id, allowing you to see which customers have taken out loans.

Each row represents a loan, including its type, the customer who borrowed it, the branch that issued it, and the loan amount. It links to the customer and the branch, providing details of each loan and which customers and branches are involved.
Each row represents a bike-sharing station, including its ID, name, location coordinates, number of docks, city, and installation date. It links to the station's current status.
Each row shows the current status of a bike station, including the number of bikes and docks available at a specific time. It links to the station table to identify which station is being monitored.
Each row represents a bike trip, recording the duration and start/end dates, stations, bike ID, subscription type, and customer's zip code. It links to no other tables but tracks individual rides.

Each row represents weather conditions for a specific day at a given zip code. It records various measurements like temperature, humidity, pressure, visibility, wind speed, and precipitation. No other tables are linked to this table.

Each row represents an entrepreneur and their request for funding. It includes the entrepreneur's ID, the person they represent, the company involved, the amount of money requested, and the investor. It links to the person associated with the entrepreneur.
Each row represents a person, recording their ID, name, height, weight and date of birth. It links to the entrepreneur table to identify entrepreneurs.

Each row represents a conductor (the musical director) identified by an ID. It includes the conductor's name, age, nationality and the year they started working with the orchestra. It links to the orchestra table, showing which conductors have worked with it.

Each row represents a visitor to the theme park, recording their unique identifier and additional details. It links to the visits table, allowing details of each visit by the same person to be connected.

Each row describes a feature or attraction within the theme park, such as rides or shows. It records detailed information about each feature. The table is referenced to list features of tourist attractions.

Each row represents a hotel within the theme park, noting its star rating, whether pets are allowed, price range, and other details. It links to the star rating definition for clarity on the hotel's quality level.

Each row describes a tourist attraction (a place of interest) in the theme park, including its type, location, how to get there, name, description, opening hours and other details. Each row describes a street market within the theme park, including its details. It links to the tourist attractions table, allowing connections between markets and other attractions in the park.
Each row represents a shop within the theme park, detailing its name or description. It links to tourist attractions, allowing you to find shops associated with specific attractions.
Each row represents a museum within the theme park, containing details about it. It links to the tourist attractions table, allowing connections between museums and other attractions in the park.
Each row represents a member of the royal family. It contains details about each member. It links to tourist attractions, showing which attractions are associated with the royal family.
Each row represents a theme park, with details about it. It links to the tourist attractions within the park, allowing you to see what attractions are part of each theme park.

Each row records a visit to a tourist attraction within the theme park. It includes the date of the visit and any details about it. It links to the tourist who visited and the attraction they visited, connecting visits with tourists and attractions.

Each row is a photo of a tourist attraction in the theme park. It records the photo's name, description, filename and any other details. It links to the tourist attraction it depicts, allowing you to match photos to attractions.
Each row represents a staff member at a theme park, including their name and any additional details. It links to the specific tourist attraction where the staff member works.

Each row links a tourist attraction to its features. It records the attraction's ID and the feature's ID, showing which attractions have which features. It connects to the tourist attractions table and allows identifying all attractions with specific features.

Each row is a tweet (a message posted on Twitter). It records the tweet's ID, the user who posted it, the text of the tweet and when it was created. It links to the user profile of the poster.
Each row is a Twitter user profile, containing the user's ID, name, email, and number of followers. It links to other tables that record who follows whom and the tweets posted by the user.

Each row represents an election result, recording the number of votes and percentage for a representative. It also notes the date, seat count, and placement in the election. It links to the representative who was elected.

Each row represents a student, recording their ID, first name, last name, age, sex, major, advisor, and city code. It links to the voting records that track how each student voted in various elections.

Each row represents a news report, linking a journalist to an event. It records the type of work done (e.g., article, video). It connects to journalists and events, showing which reporters covered what events and in what capacity.
Each row describes a type of grape used in winemaking, noting its name and color. It links to the wine table to show which grapes are used in specific wines.

Each row is an address, containing the full content of the address, city, zip code, state or province, and country. It links to the customer addresses table, allowing customers' multiple addresses to be recorded.

Each row represents a product available for sale. It contains details about the product. It links to orders that include this product, allowing you to see which products are part of specific sales transactions.

Each row represents a contact channel for a customer, such as a phone number. It records the customer ID, the type of channel, and the dates when it was active. It links to the customer who uses this channel.
